reasoning_traces.think:
The system computes a relevance score through a two-stage process: first, assigning a base weight to user feedback (rating or purchase), then adjusting it via a temporal decay factor. The feedback weight maps discrete ratings to continuous relevance values, ranging from -3 (low interest) to 5 (high interest). Multiplying by the temporal decay factor scales this relevance based on recency—items purchased recently receive higher multipliers (up to 2), while older purchases get lower ones (1). This produces a composite score that spans from -6 to 10, where negative values suggest disinterest, zero or below indicates low-rated items, and values above 5 imply actual purchases. These scores are aggregated from multiple similar item lists, summed, and sorted descendingly before filtering out irrelevant or previously interacted items. The final ranked list ensures high-quality recommendations by combining behavioral signals with temporal dynamics.
